about: Réserve du Naufraget is a Vouvray bottled under the Domaine de Vaufuget label by Maison Pierre Chainier, a family wine house based in Amboise, the royal town on the Loire where Leonardo da Vinci spent his last years. The family’s winemaking roots run back to the Bordeaux region in the mid-18th century and to Cognac in the early 20th; the Loire business dates from the 1960s, and today the family also tends estates in Touraine, including Château de la Roche and Château de Pocé.

The grapes are Chenin Blanc from Vouvray, upstream from Tours on the north bank of the Loire. Here the vines grow in clay-limestone and clay-silica soils over tuffeau, the soft chalky stone into which the village’s troglodyte cellars are carved; the roots reach down toward those very caves. The fruit is picked by hand in October, some of it touched by noble rot, which concentrates its sugar. Fermentation is deliberately slow, lasting about a month, and is stopped short of full dryness.

The result is an off-dry Vouvray: a gently sweet impression on the palate that resolves into a clean, dry-feeling finish. Expect orange peel, ripe quince and a light note of honey, the classic signature of Chenin Blanc grown on chalk, with enough acidity to keep the sweetness in balance at the table, where it meets spice, smoke and salt with ease.
